**Visual observations from the test image:**
- Close-up of a soybean leaf (likely upper surface)
- Leaf is dark green with a heavily wrinkled/rugose/puckered texture — almost blistered appearance
- Small scattered yellowish-green spots visible
- No distinct necrotic lesions, no white powdery coating, no obvious pustules
- Leaf surface appears thick and distorted

**Key matching:**
- The heavily wrinkled, dark green, thick-looking leaf strongly matches **Soybean_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus**: *"dark green, brittle, wrinkled, curled, small, and thick leaves combined with yellowing between leaf veins"*
- Powdery_Mildew ruled out (no white powder visible)
- Downy_mildew ruled out (no grayish sporulation)
- Bacterial diseases ruled out (no angular lesions with halos)

The reference collage for Soybean_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus shows field-level symptoms (stunting, yellowing, wrinkled leaves), consistent with the close-up wrinkled dark green leaf in the test image.
